1. $P_\theta(x)=\sum_z P_\theta(x,z)$ (or integral if $z$ continuous).
2. Set $P(Z=j)=\alpha_j$ and $P(x\mid Z=j)=P_{\theta_j}(x)$; marginalize $Z$ to get $\sum_j\alpha_j P_{\theta_j}(x)$.
3. Model parameters $\theta$ and a distribution over the latent $Z$ (since $z$ is unobserved).
4. No — it is a common compression choice, not a theorem requirement.
5. Direct MLE has intractable / non-closed $\log\sum$ objectives; latent structure + EM / ELBO tools handle that class.
